1) educators’ understandings and practices are shaped by the context of reform; 2) educators’ experiences are shaped by their positions within the reform; and 3) educators’ experiences shape their views of families’ role in schooling.
the lighted schoolhouse is an example of a reform that is designed to strengthen the connection between home and school but that it is not clear how this will happen.
the lighted schoolhouse is an attempt to reframe the home-school relationship in a way that is intended to be more equitable and inclusive of all families.

educators’ experiences of the reform were shaped by the ways that they were positioned in the context of the lighted schoolhouse reform.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

educators are able to use their resources and relationships in schools to support families’ engagement in their children’s education, but they are not able to use those resources and relationships to support families in the home.

while there are many opportunities to build relationships between families and educators, these opportunities are often constrained by the resources available to the school and how the school is organized to work with families.

The main takeaway from our work is that

while educators are committed to building connections between home and school, they are constrained in doing so by their limited time and resources, the ways in which they are evaluated, and the ways in which families are positioned in their communities.
educators’ views of home and school as separate spheres are challenged by the reform’s focus on the family-school connection.
educators and families’ experiences with the reform are shaped by their positions in relation to one another, as well as by how the reform is designed and implemented.
